meta.reportLabel: Spain's election is now dated to November 29 and the euro bounced off 1.1161 rather than breaking, so EUR/USD drops to MED; a 5.324% US ten-year sends gold and silver back to SHORT.
meta.coverage: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, NZD, CAD, CHF · 28 pairs (full G10 ex SEK/NOK) + DXY + JPYBASKET + GER40 + EU50 + XAU + XAG + XCU + USOIL
meta.regime: The euro's political tail risk resolved into a dated event rather than a break: Sanchez called the snap election for November 29, EUR/USD traded down to 1.1161 and then bounced to 1.12170, and the currency is now flat to higher against six of its seven counterparts. The second change is in US rates, where the ten-year pushed back to 5.3240% within two basis points of last week's 2002 high, which reversed the one-week bounce in gold and silver that this report leaned on yesterday.
meta.nextBigEvent: BoJ Governor Ueda speaks at 06:35Z today at the National Securities Convention - the week's first red folder and the only scheduled chance to put the October 30 meeting, priced near 24%, back on the table.

dailyRead: Start with the euro, because yesterday this report cut it to -1 on a specific risk and that risk has now happened. Pedro Sanchez dissolved parliament on Monday October 5 and called a general election for November 29, the earliest Sunday the law allows, after the Congress rejected his emergency housing decrees when Junts withdrew support. The thing a 4H trader has to notice is what the euro did with the confirmation: EUR/USD traded down to 1.1161, a fresh 17-month low, and then bounced, and it is 1.12170 this morning - down just 0.05% on the day and actually above yesterday's 1.11804 close. The breadth that justified the cut has also stopped. Twenty-four hours ago the euro was losing against all seven counterparts; today EUR/JPY is +0.10%, EUR/CHF +0.08%, EUR/GBP -0.01%, EUR/CAD -0.01%, EUR/AUD -0.03% and EUR/NZD -0.04%, which is a flat tape, not a rout. That is the classic shape of a political risk being sold into the announcement and bought on the fact, and the reason is that an election with a date attached is a smaller unknown than a weekend of speculation. The wires have caught up with that distinction too, with the consensus framing now that Spain is the sideshow and France is where the risk premium actually lives. So EUR stays at -1 rather than being cut again, and EUR/USD comes off HIGH conviction to MED: the structural case is intact but the momentum case is not, and defending a HIGH after the market refused the news would be carrying a stale call. What has not changed is the French leg, and it now has a date of its own. Lecornu's 2027 draft budget goes through October in committee ahead of a November 17 vote in the Assembly, the four left-wing groups have each promised censure, and the government's survival depends on how the National Rally plays it, with Article 49.3 the obvious fallback. TradingEconomics has the French ten-year at 4.8670% against a Bund at 3.4922%, so the OAT-Bund spread is about 137 basis points - a touch narrower than Friday's 141 but still the widest since 2012, with France wide of Italy at 4.6380% and Greece at 4.4870%. Spanish credit is still refusing to price the election: the ten-year is 4.1510%, about 66 basis points over the Bund, barely changed on the announcement. So the euro carries two dated political events three weeks apart, November 17 and November 29, and no bond-market confirmation of either. Trade it as a cross story rather than a dollar story, because that is where it is actually working: EUR/GBP is -0.98% on the week and EUR/CHF -1.38%, while EUR/USD is only -1.10%. The second real change today is in US rates, and it matters most outside FX. The ten-year is 5.3240% and up 1.2 basis points, which puts it within two basis points of the 5.342% intraday print last week that was the highest since 2002. Yesterday it was 5.27% and falling, and this report used that easing to move gold and silver off SHORT to RANGE on the grounds that their weekly momentum had turned positive. That rationale is now factually gone: gold is 4124.26 and -1.38% on the week against the +0.52% quoted yesterday, and silver is 60.591 and -1.40% against +0.61%. Both metals are back to SHORT, and the honest lesson is that one day of weekly momentum was too thin a basis to retire a short inside an intact downtrend - gold is still -6.37% on the month and silver -8.39%, and with August CPI at 3.4% a 5.32% ten-year leaves close to two points of real yield for a metal to beat. The dollar itself is unchanged at +2 and deliberately so. DXY is 102.185, up 0.08% on the day and 0.80% on the week, but the December case softened slightly at the margin rather than firming: CME pricing now has the October 28 hold near 78-82% and a December 9 hike at roughly 62-67%, against the 69% carried yesterday. The floor under it is still the September SEP, where sixteen of eighteen participants wanted at least one more hike this year and the 2026 median was revised up to 4.1%, against September payrolls of 29K versus an 89K forecast, unemployment at 4.2% and the fed funds upper bound at 4.00% after a 12-0 September hike. FOMC minutes tomorrow at 18:00Z are the test of whether that 62-67% holds, and they are the only scheduled US red folder of the week. Sterling is the cleanest long-side story on the board and it firmed again overnight, this time from the Governor himself. Bailey has now said in public that persistently high energy prices make holding Bank Rate harder to justify, which is a different thing from the three dissenters wanting 4.00%, and the market-implied probability of a November 5 hike moved to about 85% on the BoE Watch measure from roughly 70% before his remarks. Oxford Economics has joined Barclays, UBS and J.P. Morgan, and goes further: November and February, taking Bank Rate to 4.25%. The pass-through argument is mechanical - UK gas is 186.21 GBp/thm, up 5.48% on the week and 152.28% year to date, after the domestic unit rate stepped up about 27% year on year on October 1 - and the gilt ten-year at 5.4049% is above the US ten-year and near a two-decade high. GBP stays at +2 rather than going to +3 for two reasons worth stating: the labour leg is genuinely soft, with unemployment at 4.9%, the payroll proxy at -26.1K and wage growth decelerating to 3.9%, and at 85% priced the November hike is largely in the price, so the marginal sterling upside now sits in the February extension rather than in November itself. Bailey speaks again on October 8 at 12:15Z and that is a red folder; Mann is at 08:30Z today. The yen is the one position where the next hour matters more than the last day. USD/JPY is 158.144, up 0.15% today and 0.54% on the week, and Ueda speaks at 06:35Z at the National Securities Convention. Market pricing going in is roughly 24% for the October 30 meeting and about 60% for a hike by year-end, against a policy rate of 1.25% after the 7-2 September 18 hike with Asada and Sato dissenting. The setup is asymmetric in the sense that the dovish outcome is already the base case, so a hawkish signal has more room to move the tape than a neutral one - but the structural drag is unmoved, with 1.25% against a 5.3240% US ten-year still the worst funding disadvantage on this board even after the JGB ten-year rose to 3.1110%. JPY holds at 0 into the speech, and the yen crosses carry LOW-MED conviction on event proximity rather than on any thesis weakness. Tonight's average cash earnings at 23:30Z is the second risk, and the forecast is a sharp deceleration to 3.7% from 4.7%, which would undercut the wage leg the BoJ leans on. The franc continues to validate yesterday's upgrade, which is worth saying because the upgrade was a correction. Over the past week USD/CHF fell 0.28% while DXY rose 0.80% - the franc beat a dollar that beat almost everything else - and the franc-funded crosses kept falling: EUR/CHF -1.38%, NZD/CHF -1.05%, CAD/CHF -0.81% and AUD/CHF -0.51%. CHF holds at 0, capped rather than sunk by a 0.00% policy rate against a Swiss ten-year of 0.5270% and an SNB that has restored its willingness to intervene, with nothing scheduled before December 10. Commodities are where yesterday's calls need the most honesty. The WTI-Brent spread was the trade: it was 11.48 dollars on Friday and the thesis was that the G7 and IEA release of up to 100 million barrels, front-loaded over twenty days into US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude and diesel, would keep widening it. It narrowed instead. WTI is 89.785 and up 0.40% today and 0.45% on the week; Brent is 100.682 and up 0.36% and 4.70%; the spread is about 10.90 dollars. The location call is not working, so USOIL goes back to RANGE. What has not changed at all is the physical premium underneath both: the Strait of Hormuz is in day 219 of closure, there was a single commercial transit on September 27 against roughly 85 a day before the crisis, around 200 vessels are holding position, and war-risk insurance is running at about thirty times normal with VLCC quotes reaching ten million dollars. Copper has its own new fact and it cuts against Australia. BHP requested mandatory government mediation at Escondida on Monday October 5, which suspends the strike the 1,020-member supervisors' union authorised on a 95% vote after rejecting the contract offer on October 1. Mediation runs five days and can be extended by five more, so the supply disruption that was the bullish kicker is deferred to roughly October 10-15, and copper is 6.5965 dollars a pound, up only 0.17% today and 0.81% on the week against -2.11% on the month. XCU stays RANGE and AUD stays at 0, with a 4.60% cash rate, August CPI at 4.0% headline and 3.6% core, unemployment up to 4.6%, and November 3 priced near one in three. Canada is the only board member with red-folder figures this week and the forecast has been revised down: September employment on Friday October 9 at 12:30Z is now seen at +6.2K after -41.7K, with the unemployment rate expected to rise to 6.5% from 6.4%. CAD holds at -1 on a 2.25% overnight rate, 175 basis points below the Fed, and the terms-of-trade problem is unchanged even as the spread narrows, because Canada sells into the discounted barrel. New Zealand stays at -1 and weakest, with NZD/USD at 0.55984 and -0.77% on the week, the worst of the majors, an OCR of 2.75% and Q3 CPI on October 21 as the clean test against the Bank's own published 3.9% forecast; TradingEconomics now carries a forecast of 3.00% for the December 9 meeting, which is the first real hawkish marker on that curve. Equities are the quiet disappointment. DE40 is 25,319.00 and up 0.09% today but down 2.64% on the week, which is the leg that breaks yesterday's modest long: the weak-euro translation story and sub-ninety WTI were both supposed to pay and the index did not pay, so GER40 returns to RANGE even with German gas easing 1.71% on the day. EU50 is 6,264.50, up 0.04% and down 2.18% on the week, and it stays RANGE on its own evidence: the bank weight benefits from a steep curve and a hawkish ECB while the French political leg does not, and the periphery is still the tell, with Spain's ES35 up 1.12% and 24.06% year to date and Italy's IT40 up 17.78%, rallying straight through the same politics that is sinking the currency. The clean trades are unchanged at the top and that is the point: EUR/GBP short at 0.84874 is still the highest-conviction idea on the board with both legs moving the right way and -0.98% on the week, GBP/NZD long at 2.36067 is the widest policy spread available at +0.65%, and EUR/CHF short at 0.93281 is working at -1.38%. EUR/USD short is demoted to MED because the market refused the news, and the two metals shorts are back on because the ten-year refused to fall. Not financial advice.

geopolitics: The oil transmission is unchanged underneath and wrong on the surface, which is the opposite of yesterday. The physical picture has not improved at all: the Strait of Hormuz is in day 219 of closure, there was a single commercial transit on September 27 against roughly 85 a day before the crisis, about 200 vessels are holding position away from berth, war-risk insurance is running at about thirty times normal premium with VLCC voyage quotes reaching ten million dollars against 250,000 in peacetime, and four of the nine largest global carriers have stopped using the strait entirely. That is the structural bid under crude and it is why being short oil is a dangerous expression of anything. What has changed is that the trade built on top of it stopped working. Yesterday this report moved USOIL to SHORT on a location call: the G7, IEA and partner release of up to 100 million barrels agreed October 2 is front-loaded over twenty days and comes out of US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude and diesel rather than waterborne barrels, so the WTI-Brent spread at 11.48 dollars was supposed to keep widening. It narrowed to about 10.90 instead. WTI is 89.785 and up 0.40% today and 0.45% on the week; Brent is 100.682 and up 0.36% and 4.70%, so both legs rose and the discounted barrel rose slightly faster. USOIL therefore goes back to RANGE, and the lesson is that a spread thesis needs the spread, not the level, to confirm. Gas is still the leg with no relief and it is the inflation engine. EU gas is 74.95 EUR/MWh and up 1.96% today, 7.89% on the week and 166.16% year to date; UK gas is 186.21 GBp/thm and up 1.43% today, 5.48% on the week and 152.28% year to date; German gas is the one softening, down 1.71% today to 74.47 and up only 0.50% on the week. The FX read follows the asymmetry. Sterling is the clearest beneficiary, and the argument got its strongest endorsement yet when Bailey said in public that persistently high energy prices make holding Bank Rate harder to justify - that took November 5 from roughly 70% to about 85% and brought Oxford Economics in alongside Barclays, UBS and J.P. Morgan, with the domestic unit rate having stepped up about 27% year on year on October 1. Canada gets the mirror image: it sells into the barrel that trades 10.90 dollars under Brent, which keeps CAD at -1 into Friday's September employment report, now forecast at +6.2K after -41.7K with unemployment seen rising to 6.5%. The euro imports the gas shock into a 3.8% HICP it cannot monetise, because the Council will not tighten into a bloc carrying a November 17 French budget vote the left has promised to censure and a November 29 Spanish election - but note that the euro bounced when that election was confirmed, because a dated event is smaller than an open-ended one, and the intra-European haven bid is still going into the franc rather than out of Europe. Copper is the new piece and it points the other way from where it was. BHP requested mandatory government mediation at Escondida on October 5, suspending the strike that the 1,020-member supervisors' union had authorised on a 95% vote, so the supply disruption that was the bullish kicker for copper and for AUD is deferred to roughly October 10-15 rather than live. Copper is 6.5965 and up only 0.17%. For the dollar the energy premium is a yield story that is working again: the ten-year is back at 5.3240% and up 1.2 basis points, within two basis points of last week's 5.342% high, the highest since 2002, and that is precisely what sent gold and silver back to SHORT after one day at RANGE. Equities are taking neither the oil relief nor the gas threat and simply drifting - DE40 is +0.09% today but -2.64% on the week and EU50 +0.04% and -2.18% - while the periphery indices keep outperforming, with Spain's ES35 up 24.06% year to date through its own election.
